notes:
A popup lets you know when a tracker seems to be following you. Tracker monitoring is in Settings, and both warnings stay off until you turn one on. Separated tag with you warns when a tag says it is away from its owner, this phone has heard it for 30 minutes with no gap over 20 minutes, and GPS has three places at least 100 m apart. Heard at two places warns when a finder with a stable address reaches two stops. There is no beep. Open radio opens that radio. Dismiss keeps that warning down while the same condition continues. A quiet notification shows the same lines when Fieldwatch is not on screen.

These warnings are a guide, not proof. Fieldwatch will not catch every tracker, and a warning does not mean someone is tracking you. If you think you are in danger, contact local law enforcement.

Pebblebee also matches Bluetooth service FA25. A tag that leaves its name off still matches. Google Find Hub shows a 20-byte or 32-byte ephemeral id. Frame 0x40 is labeled not separated. A Find My advertisement of 25 bytes says it is broadcasting a public key. A 2-byte advertisement says it is the short form, often a tag near its owner, and that this is not certain. The battery level shows only when the recent-owner bit is set.

Exposure Notification names a Bluetooth advertisement on service FD6F and leaves the identifier and the metadata off the page. BTHome shows the measurements a sensor advertises, and an open door or window shows on the live row. Amazon Sidewalk shows the beacon type and the battery band, and registration mode shows on the live row. An Echo without that service stays Amazon. Matter setup shows the vendor ID, the product ID, and the discriminator, and proximity ranging leaves the hidden id off the page. HomeKit names the category and the paired line. An unpaired accessory shows that category on the live row. None of these beep.

Remote ID authentication shows the type, page, and time the plate sends. The signature bytes stay off the page and are not checked. A location message in the same session keeps that block. French Direct Remote ID can fill the aircraft position, altitude, speed, course, and the takeoff pin when that Wi-Fi beacon is present. Height above takeoff shows on the radio page and is not the aircraft pin. Android 11 or newer.

A Wi-Fi access point can say what kind of network it is, whether it has internet, a venue, and a hotspot id. Detail shows that when the beacon includes it. The access point sets these. They are not checked. Compare and Debrief keep the percent moving on a large sit. Compare (text) and Debrief (text) share a text file. If a share cannot open, Fieldwatch says why.

Bundled language files are written for this version. A language file can be up to 352 KiB.
